english.title: Fail without reasonable excuse to provide information required by authority in notice under s19(2)
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) having been served by notice in writing by

(A)_[the Secretary of State,]_
(B)_[a local enforcing authority, namely **(..NAME OF THE AUTHORITY..),]_
(C)_[the Environment Agency,]_
(D)_[the Scottish Environment Protection Agency]_

failed without reasonable excuse to comply with a requirement imposed by that notice under section 19(2) of the Environmental Protection Act 1990, to furnish to that authority information, namely **(..SPECIFY THE REQUIREMENT BREACHED..), within such a period or at such time as specified in the notice
english.legislation: Contrary to section 23(1)(g) and (3) of the Environmental Protection Act 1990.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
served with s. 19(2) notice in writing
fail to furnish to the authority information specified
in form and within such period
following service of the notice / at such time as was specified

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: (i) The 'authority' can be (a) the Secretary of State, (b) a local enforcing authority, (c) the Environment Agency or (d) SEPA

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine

Time limit for prosecution:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
